'''Socca''' (French), '''torta di ceci''' or '''farinata''' (Italian), is a type of [[Cookbook:Flatbread|flatbread]] made from chickpea flour.

''See also: [[Cookbook:Calentita|Calentita]]''

==Ingredients==

* 300 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]]) [[Cookbook:Chickpea Flour|chickpea flour]]
* 500 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] (2 cups) [[Cookbook:Water|water]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* [[Cookbook:Pepper|Black pepper]] to taste; 2–3 decent grinds of a grinder should do

==Equipment==

* [[Cookbook:Oven|Oven]]
* Something to cook the ''socca'' on; traditionally, a 50cm (20 inch) copper plaque is used as it spreads the heat evenly to all parts of the ''socca'', but a good [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|cast iron pan]] will suffice if preheated in the oven first. 

==Procedure==
# Heat oven as high as it can go—around 300°C / 570°F is traditional, but do whatever your oven can manage that gets close to this. If using a cast-iron pan, get it into the oven at the start so that it is hot when the batter goes into it.
# [[Cookbook:Whisk|Whisk]] all the ingredients together well, ensuring there are no lumps. This should make a very thin, easy-to-pour batter.
# Once the oven is up to temperature, pour some of the batter into the hot pan or onto the plaque, and put into the oven for 8–9 minutes at 300°C / 570°F, or 13–15 minutes at 250°C / 480°F. With a 50 cm plaque or pan, cook half the batter at a time—the batter should cover the plaque or pan very thinly.
# Remove from the oven and cut into triangular wedges. Serve hot.
# Repeat for the rest of the batter.
